title: Three GTM Engines, One India Base

headline.label: India IT spending in 2026 — up 10.6% year on year

engines.what: India's large domestic corporates — and the India operations of global enterprises — buying enterprise technology at scale. This is where platform value is proven, where committees decide, and where references are born.
engines.why: India is the world's fourth-largest economy at roughly US$4.5 trillion (IMF, October 2025), and its enterprises are compounding technology spend at double-digit rates. Enterprise buying here is committee-led and relationship-led — trust, credibility and patience decide outcomes — which is exactly the motion Pivora is built to run.
outlook: India IT spending is projected to reach roughly US$203B by 2028 — a 10.5% five-year CAGR, among the fastest of any major economy (Gartner IT Spending Forecast, India).
IT services spending growth is expected to average 12–14% over the next few years, led by cloud, AI/ML, cybersecurity and application modernisation (Gartner, November 2025).
Enterprise software is the fastest-compounding line — AI-enabled applications are becoming the default purchase, not the exception (Gartner, November 2025).
engines.pivora: How Pivora works this GTM: named-account architecture, trust-led executive access, and lighthouse wins engineered to become references.
engines.sources: Gartner, India IT Spending Forecast (November 2025); Gartner IT Spending Forecast, India, 2Q24 update; IMF World Economic Outlook (October 2025).

headline.label: GCC's in India, FY2026 — and still accelerating

engines.what: Global Capability Centres: the captive centres global enterprises run in India. They are no longer back offices — they hold product, portfolio and AI mandates for the parent enterprise, and they buy like headquarters.
engines.why: A win inside a GCC's is never a domestic win. 96% of GCC's set up after FY2021 launched with a product or portfolio mandate, and over 1,200 already run embedded AI/ML capability (Nasscom–Zinnov, May 2026). One India proof replicates into the parent's global estate — this is how India coverage becomes global coverage.

today.note: Forbes Global 2000 companies with India GCC's

outlook: The ecosystem is on course to cross US$100B in annual revenue by 2030, with around 2,400 centres employing up to 3.5 million professionals (Nasscom).

Nearly 70% of GCC's already run a defined AI roadmap and are shifting from scale execution to strategic ownership of critical functions (Nasscom Strategic Review 2026) — buying platforms, not just talent.
The next wave is mid-market global companies and new sectors — retail, healthcare, pharma — setting up their first India centres (Nasscom–Zinnov).
engines.pivora: How Pivora works this GTM: GCC opportunity mapping, mandate-aligned propositions, and wins engineered from day one to replicate globally.
engines.sources: Nasscom–Zinnov, India GCC Landscape 2026 (May 2026); Nasscom, Strategic Review 2026; Nasscom, India GCC Landscape — The 5-Year Journey.

engines.what: Global System Integrators: the Tier-1 and Tier-2 service providers headquartered out of India — TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCLTech, Tech Mahindra and the Tier-2 bench — who carry platforms into thousands of enterprise accounts worldwide.
engines.why: A GSI's alliance is the highest-leverage route an enterprise platform can take from India: one activated partnership multiplies into every account the integrator serves. Most platforms sign the agreement and stop there. Almost none build the joint pipeline, the enabled teams and the co-sell cadence that turn a logo into revenue.

today.note: Industry revenue, FY2026 (+6.1%) — Nasscom Strategic Review 2026

outlook: Nasscom projects India's technology industry to roughly double to US$500B by 2030 — with GSI's carrying that growth into global enterprise accounts.
AI is moving from pilots to scaled, outcome-led deployment — 90% of global technology buyers plan to increase AI allocations within digital budgets (Nasscom Global CXO Survey, 2026).
ER&D and AI-embedded services are the fastest-growing pillars — exactly the work GSI's need differentiated platform partners for (Nasscom Strategic Review 2026).
engines.pivora: How Pivora works this GTM: partner proposition design, alliance activation and joint account motions — signed logos converted into pipeline.
engines.sources: Nasscom, Technology Sector Strategic Review 2026 (February 2026); Nasscom Strategic Review 2023 (US$500B-by-2030 trajectory); Nasscom Global End User CXO Survey, 2026.

caption: Whichever of the three you sell to, the same India base carries the other two.
